title: Evaluation of postoperative outcomes and quality of life in patients with arterial-popliteal compression syndrome
summary: Popliteal artery compression syndrome is the compression of the knee artery, which leads to reduced blood flow in the patient's lower leg and feet. This causes symptoms from slight restrictions in walking distance to an acute vital threat to the lower leg with the risk of amputation. As the clinical picture often manifests itself in different and varied ways, it is often underdiagnosed. The results of surgical treatment are highly variable and individual. In order to gain insights into the long-term success of surgical treatment and thus improve the quality of care for affected patients, the surgical treatment and quality of life after the operation are examined and evaluated in this study.
conditions: popliteal entrapment syndrome, arterial-popliteal compression syndrome

interventions.name: Retrospective study of the surgical treatment and prospective evaluation of the postoperative quality of life of patients with arterial-popliteal compression syndrome who were treated surgically in our Clinic for Vascular Surgery and Endovascular Surgery.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patient's ability to give consent, surgical treatment due to a PAE has taken place
Exclusion criteria:
Underage patients, patients unable to give consent
